correctness.rationale: Represent white pairs as edge graph H on base labels. For blue pair uv, its number of white neighbors equals d_H(u)+d_H(v) because uv is absent; a unique white neighbor exists exactly for an isolated endpoint and degree-one endpoint. Thus every force removes a white leaf edge. With no isolate no first force; a white cycle cannot lose its first edge under the rule, proving necessity. If H is a forest with isolate z, use blue edge uz with a leaf u to force its sole white incident edge, iterating; sufficiency is constructive. Maximum white edges n-2 gives Z=binom(n,2)-n+2 and exactly n(n-1)^{n-3} Cayley trees with isolated vertex. Labeled-forest exponential assembly with at least one singleton proves the entire polynomial. Between isolates r!=s, exchange iff deleting the unique edge incident to s and adding unique edge incident to r leaves common tree U on n-2 others; choose U and two attachment labels, giving binom(n,2)(n-2)^{n-2} cross-class edges. Within-isolate usual spanning-tree exchange connected; star-switch crosses classes. Independent line-graph forcing and forest-isolate exhaustive checks for n=3..6, plus cross-class counts, agree; universal iff rests on the local degree lemma.

value.rationale: The triangular graphs are a canonical association-scheme and line-graph family. A single structural forest-and-isolate criterion solves the natural decision problem for every initially blue set, yields a full exact enumerator beyond the known optimum, and describes how all Cayley-tree minimizers interconvert by token jumping, with explicit cross-fibre edges. These are natural structural invariants, not a restatement of the prior scalar minimum.

limitations: n>=3 triangular graphs only; not all Johnson or arbitrary line graphs.
